business_question: How much do rankings change across scenarios?
finding_statement: The median CMA's rank range across the four scenarios is 6; the largest is 20 (Toronto); scenario rank correlations with balanced range from 0.85 to 0.95.

limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability

business_question: Is the framework dominated by market size?
finding_statement: Score and log scale correlate at balanced 0.58, growth-led 0.30, stability-aware 0.55 (Spearman), below the declared 0.8 threshold; the scale-led scenario reaches 0.91 and C01 explains 81% of its score variance, so the scale-led scenario is essentially a size ordering.
evidence_measure: Spearman(score, log scale); component variance share
population: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
evidence_eligibility: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Balanced, growth-led and stability-aware scores are not restatements of size; read the scale-led scenario as a size view

finding_statement: Raw volatility is strongly related to size (Spearman -0.645); after scale adjustment it is not (-0.041). An unadjusted penalty would move the smallest-quartile markets by +1.78 ranks on average versus -0.62 for others; stability-aware ranks differ little from balanced.
population: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
evidence_eligibility: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Keep volatility as a confidence measure and a limited scale-adjusted component, not a core penalty

business_question: Does commercial fit materially change conclusions?
finding_statement: Removing commercial fit moves balanced ranks by 4 places at the median and up to 12 (Quebec); it counterweights scale and dynamism (Spearman with C03 -0.739).
population: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
evidence_eligibility: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Commercial fit is material; its definition (20-99 locations) should be reviewed with sales strategy

business_question: Does any pillar gain hidden influence?
finding_statement: The momentum pillar explains 38% of balanced score variance against a 25% nominal weight. Its two components are averaged, so the excess comes from momentum being nearly independent of the other pillars, while dynamism and commercial fit partly offset each other (Spearman -0.739).
evidence_measure: variance share of the momentum pillar
population: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
evidence_eligibility: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Momentum differentiates markets more than its weight suggests; pair momentum-led readings with the signal-clarity measure

business_question: How reliable is the momentum signal?
finding_statement: Only 3 of 35 CMAs have a 12-month mean net-formation rate clearly distinguishable from month-to-month noise; 14 of 14 momentum-led classifications (across scenarios) rest on an unclear 12-month signal.
population: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
evidence_eligibility: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Treat momentum-led placements as provisional; pair with the 36-month trend and internal data

business_question: Which Tier 3 markets deserve separate qualitative review?
finding_statement: The six scale-only CMAs rank between the 2.5th and 22.5th 41-CMA scale percentile; the largest are Nanaimo, Kamloops. They have no momentum evidence and are not scored.
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Review qualitatively (for example with local market knowledge) rather than by score

business_question: What internal data is needed before final acquisition-investment decisions?
finding_statement: The score covers external evidence only. A decision needs current market share and customers, branch coverage, relationship-manager capacity, credit risk appetite, acquisition cost, conversion history and customer profitability.
population: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
evidence_eligibility: full framework: 35 CMAs with complete 0722 momentum history
limitation: External public-aggregate signal only; excludes bank market share, customers, branches, RM capacity, credit risk, acquisition cost, conversion and profitability
implication: Next: combine with (synthetic, later) internal evidence; the external score alone does not set investment
